ai.subject: Anatomy
ai.summary: The jejunum is the middle section of the small intestine, responsible for nutrient absorption and mixing chyme with digestive enzymes. It is richly vascularized and innervated, making it a common site for infections and inflammatory conditions.

sections.p: The jejunum lies between the duodenum and ileum, about 2.5 m long in adults. It is the main site for absorption of most nutrients and electrolytes.
It starts at the ligament of Treitz and ends at the ileocecal valve. The wall has thick mucosa with many folds (plicae circulares) and a prominent submucosal lymphoid tissue.
Anteriorly it lies on the pancreas and posteriorly on the mesenteric vessels. The mesentery supplies blood and lymphatics.
Supplied by the jejunal branches of the superior mesenteric artery; drained by jejunal veins into the portal system.
b: Vein: jejunal veins to portal vein

sections.p: Parasympathetic via vagus and pelvic splanchnic nerves; sympathetic via mesenteric plexus.
Primary role is absorption of carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, and minerals. It also secretes digestive enzymes and hormones like CCK.
Common problems include bacterial overgrowth, Crohn’s disease, ischemia, and parasitic infections. Symptoms are abdominal pain, diarrhea, and malabsorption.

sections.p: Remember that the jejunum is the site of most nutrient absorption and is highly vascular. In low-resource settings, malabsorption often results from infections like malaria or schistosomiasis.

Identifies bleeding from ulcers or parasites

whenToSeekHelp: Severe abdominal pain with vomiting, signs of peritonitis, sudden weight loss, or persistent diarrhea with dehydration

faq.q: What is the main difference between jejunum and ileum?
faq.a: Jejunum absorbs most nutrients and has more villi; ileum mainly absorbs bile salts and vitamin B12.

faq.q: Why is CCK released in the jejunum?
faq.a: CCK is secreted by I-cells in response to fats and proteins to stimulate gallbladder contraction and pancreatic enzyme release.

faq.q: Can parasites live in the jejunum?
faq.a: Yes, parasites like Schistosoma mansoni eggs and certain protozoa can lodge in the jejunal lumen.
